It is building software by prompting AI, without requirements, design, testing, or structure. You feel the vibe, you ship the code. Also, there exist the Danger of Web Apps Without Software Engineering which include No Security: No proper authentication, validation, or data protection. User data leaks easily. No Structure:No planning means messy code that no one can fix or upgrade. No Testing: If it was not tested, you do not know when it will fail. It will fail in production, with real users. No Scalability. It works for 10 users, it crashes for 1,000 users.

articles.title: Track Kalshi Prediction Market Odds in Python (Fed Rate Probabilities, Volume and Price History)
articles.excerpt: Prediction markets put a price on questions like "Will the Fed hike in December?" or "How many rate cuts this year?". On Kalshi, a regulated US prediction market, each contract pays $1 if the outcome…
articles.body: Prediction markets put a price on questions like "Will the Fed hike in December?" or "How many rate cuts this year?". On Kalshi, a regulated US prediction market, each contract pays $1 if the outcome happens, so a price of $0.70 reads as roughly a 70% chance. If you follow macro news, build forecasting models or just want to see how the market's view changed after a speech or a data release, you want those prices in a table, with a history. Kalshi has a public market data API, and it's free. The work is in the glue. The API has no text search, so to find "every Fed market" you page through events and their nested markets and filter them yourself. Prices come back as dollar strings in fields like yes_bid_dollars .

articles.body: A first payment that works in sandbox can hide what happens when the next charge fails. Fail a renewal in your test environment and watch the result. Does access stay open, end at once, or follow a grace period you actually chose? Providers usually retry the card and send failed-payment or past-due events. If those arrive and your handler returns 200 without changing anything, a customer may keep a paid feature for free, or lose it with no warning. Check the notice you'd send them too. A silent change after a failed charge is how angry tickets start.

articles.title: I measured what my Claude Code setup costs on every request. Most of my skills had gone blank.
articles.excerpt: Claude Code sent 74,500 tokens with my first message of the day, before it had read a single word I typed. About 22,000 of those came from plugins, skills, MCP servers and hooks I had installed over a…
articles.body: Claude Code sent 74,500 tokens with my first message of the day, before it had read a single word I typed. About 22,000 of those came from plugins, skills, MCP servers and hooks I had installed over a few months, most of which I had forgotten about. That overhead is resent on every turn of every session. It drains your usage limit, fills the context window sooner (so sessions compact earlier), and, as it turns out, quietly makes Claude worse at picking the right skill. Here's how I measured it, the one finding that surprised me, and the small open-source tool I built so you can check your own setup. Where the numbers come from Claude Code writes a transcript of every session to ~/.claude/projects/<project>/<session>.jsonl .

articles.body: We've had no shortage of great Warhammer 40K games lately, but most aren't exactly aimed at the casual crowd. Warhammer Survivors changes that, finally providing curious gamers with an easy entry point into the grim darkness of the 41st millennium. Developed by Auroch Digital (in collaboration with Vampire Survivors' Poncle), this new spin on the survivors-like roguelite subgenre mixes the sci-fi 40,000 setting with the pure fantasy Age of Sigmar universe. This means heroes and enemies from all over the Warhammer mythos meet together in a bite-sized game that anyone can figure out and enjoy in less than five minutes. When you look at the alternatives, that's a remarkable achievement for a franchise that's notoriously hard (and often expensive) to get into .

articles.body: On Thursday (Nov. 12), the Euclid space telescope released its first major batch of data, capturing the light of more than a billion objects over an area of sky as big as 9,500 full moons. The data release lays the foundation for one of the largest-ever 3D maps of the cosmos and many groundbreaking discoveries about the nature of dark energy and dark matter. The European Space Agency 's (ESA) Euclid space telescope has been called the "Dark Universe Detective" because of its capability to investigate the dual mysteries of dark matter , the universe's most mysterious stuff, and dark energy , the force accelerating the expansion of the universe. Collectively, these cosmic elements are sometimes referred to as the dark universe.

articles.title: The replicants are running the city in thrilling final trailer for ‘Blade Runner 2099’ (video)
articles.excerpt: 'Humans are always the same. Desperate. Volatile.'
articles.body: One of the most anticipated fall TV series, " Blade Runner 2099 , " recently dropped its final neon-tinted trailer, and now we’ve finally got a handle on the plot dynamics of this dystopian thriller set in the cyberpunk world of Ridley Scott's original. Prime Video's bold and brooding 8-episode series lands Nov. 25 as a tangential sequel to Denis Villeneuve's "Blade Runner 2049," unfolding some 50 years after the 2017 feature film. Now the artificial inmates are running the asylum when violent replicant uprisings flip the script, causing humanity to become second-class citizens. "In Los Angeles 2099, Cora (Hunter Schafer) lived her entire life on the run, a chameleon forced to adopt numerous identities," states Prime Video's synopsis.

articles.title: Satellite snaps rare birds-eye view of the ISS | Space photo of the day for Nov. 12, 2026
articles.excerpt: A commercial satellite has spotted the International Space Station, giving us a unique view of the orbiting lab from above.
articles.body: A satellite looks down at the International Space Station in orbit. (Image credit: HEO) A commercial satellite has spotted the International Space Station (ISS), giving us a unique view of the orbiting lab from above. What is it? Most of the time, when we see the ISS, it is from down here on Earth or from the viewpoint of the astronauts onboard, peering out the windows at the station's limbs, solar arrays and instruments. But in this snapshot, which was posted on X on Nov. 9 by the Australian company HEO, we can see the station stretched out in all its glory. HEO specializes in using satellites in low Earth orbit to capture images of other spacecraft, though longer-term the company aims to capture observations far out into the solar system.
articles.author: Chelsea Gohd

articles.title: I used the Vaonis Vespera 3 for weeks and here’s who I would recommend it to — full review
articles.excerpt: I photographed nebulas and star clusters over multiple nights with the Vaonis Vespera 3. It’s one of the most capable smart telescopes I’ve used, but it won’t be for everyone.
articles.body: I’ve spent a lot of time with smart telescopes , from relatively inexpensive Seestar models to the original Vaonis Vespera and the Vespera Pro . They all promise essentially the same thing — you put a telescope outside at night, choose something interesting on your smartphone and let the technology take care of the rest. The Vaonis Vespera 3 does that exceptionally well, but after spending several nights with it, I’m convinced it’s designed for a rather different kind of buyer. The telescope’s optical arm folds into its curved body when switched off. (Image credit: Jamie Carter) At $2,490/£2,199, this is hardly an impulse purchase for the beginner who’s curious about astronomy – you could buy several perfectly capable smart telescopes for the same money.
